clue.text: Churchill's artful aid, for example

parts.note: both Churchill (ch, ch) and artful aid (a, a) repeat their opening sounds, so the clue is itself a specimen of the rhetorical device

explanation.surface: A crafty helper of Winston Churchill, given as an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the opening sounds of neighbouring words is a rhetorical device, shown by both Churchill and artful aid.

clue.text: Rindless ham is in need of flavouring

indicators.note: rindless strips the outer layer, leaving only the inner letter of ham
in places the word is inside need

explanation.surface: Ham with its rind cut off needs some seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IS inside NEED to give NISEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds of anise give a liquorice taste used to season food and drinks.

clue.text: Student quarter in Kings

indicators.note: in puts the quarter inside the pair of kings

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
R stands for rex, Latin for king
NE, north-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An undergraduate lodges in a district of King's College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kings' supplies two kings, LEAR and R; 'in' puts NE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is someone still being taught a skill or subject.

clue.text: International trial marriage

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: Two nations agree to a trial marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and rugby, the top-level game between two national sides.

clue.text: Test, for instance, the overdrive revs a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of the following words, run together

explanation.surface: Testing a car, the overdrive makes the engine race a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a Hampshire trout stream in England, so 'Test' is an example, not an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Test is a chalk stream in Hampshire, England, famed for trout fishing.

clue.text: Untidy woman novelist, without direction

indicators.note: without means the direction is dropped from the name

parts.note: Anthony Trollope wrote the Victorian Barchester novels
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman writer has lost her way.
explanation.definitionFit: An old insult for a slovenly or promiscuous female.

clue.text: Had too much to make speech about wartime celebration

indicators.note: about means the speech-making word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Gorged so much he had to give a speech at the victory party.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating to excess means consuming more food than one needs.

clue.text: Accuse oriental rebel falsely in famous case

indicators.note: falsely means put wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Falsely accusing an Eastern dissident becomes a notorious trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for a controversial trial or affair that draws wide public attention.

clue.text: Napoleon was their leader

parts.note: in Orwell's farmyard fable the pig Napoleon takes charge of the creatures who drove out the farmer, not the French emperor's troops

explanation.surface: The French emperor headed a group of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's farmyard fable the pig Napoleon rules the farm's beasts after their revolt.

clue.text: Passionate although not evil disposition

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement: the letters of 'not evil' are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fiery in temper, yet with no wickedness in their nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like a noun for temperament, but it signals rearranging NOTEVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe intense, forceful feeling that can boil over into fury.

clue.text: Characters in Engels' text he disguised as ladies

indicators.note: disguised means these letters appear in another form

explanation.surface: Letters in Engels's writing that he dressed up as women.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned collective term for women as a whole.

clue.text: Ulcer manifestation starts on the back bone

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

indicators.note: starts of these two words means their opening letters

explanation.surface: A sign of an ulcer begins on the patient's backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes U and M from Ulcer and manifestation; 'on' puts them after STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Again let free

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to let property is to lease it

explanation.surface: Rent the place out once more, or set someone loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a captive is to set them loose.

clue.text: Drink makes policemen sound hesitant

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
er is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Alcohol leaves the officers stammering.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented apple juice is a popular alcoholic beverage in Britain.

clue.text: Hunter, perhaps, has close call with firearm

parts.note: 'Time!' is the barman's call at closing time in a British pub
piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A huntsman narrowly escapes being shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close call' suggests a near miss, but it is the pub landlord's shout at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged metal lid protecting its face.

clue.text: Having changed name, I'm Paul, in charge of the town

indicators.note: having changed signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paul changed his name and now runs the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having changed' mixes N, IM, PAUL and IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a borough's local civic government.

clue.text: I take part in the naval manoeuvre in a big ship

indicators.note: I taking part in the shuffled group puts that letter among them
a manoeuvre moves things about, so the letters of 'the naval' are shuffled

explanation.surface: I join a fleet exercise aboard an enormous vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges THENAVAL to LEVATHAN; 'take part in' then puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sea monster's name is used for any vessel of enormous size.

clue.text: Having a brush against university side before long

indicators.note: before puts these pieces ahead of the next one

parts.note: v, versus, means against
L, left, is a side
to pine is to long

explanation.surface: A painter takes on a college team before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brush' suggests a painter or a skirmish, but it is a fox's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's bushy tail is called its brush, and this adjective means foxlike.

clue.text: An alternative to this place in Westminster

definitions.text: An alternative to this place in Westminster

parts.words: An alternative to this place in Westminster
parts.note: by parliamentary custom each House avoids naming the other chamber, referring to it only as a different place

explanation.definitionFit: Members of each House of Parliament politely refer to the other chamber with this phrase meaning a different one.

clue.text: Fashionable society trade centre

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade

explanation.surface: A stylish club opens a shopping hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chic and well turned out is in vogue.

clue.text: Treacherous person toyed with Pharaoh

definitions.meaning: a snake in the grass, someone who betrays
the asp Cleopatra, Egypt's last Pharaoh, handled to end her life

explanation.definitionFit: A snake suits both: slang for a betrayer, and the asp that Cleopatra, a Pharaoh, played with.

clue.text: Superseded by contract sale

definitions.meaning: the older card game of bridge, with bidding for trumps, gave way to contract bridge in the 1920s
a public sale where buyers bid against one another

explanation.definitionFit: Bidding links both: a public sale by competitive bids, and the earlier bridge game replaced by contract bridge.

clue.text: Left-winger returned by many votes

indicators.note: by means set beside, here followed by the next piece
returned means this word is read back to front

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, Britain's left-wing party
lots means many

explanation.surface: A socialist is re-elected with a large number of votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Each slip cast in an election is a vote, often made in secret.

clue.text: 'Tis required to stay awake

parts.note: the word sit turned backwards spells tis, and in a down entry 'up' signals that turning

explanation.surface: It is necessary to keep from sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, a word plus an upward direction, makes 'Tis.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay out of bed late into the night is to keep from sleeping.

clue.text: Apollo at Delphi, for example, caught the first boat

indicators.note: first says this piece goes at the front

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Apollo spoke through the Delphic shrine, the most famous prophetic shrine of Greece

explanation.surface: The god of Delphi, caught out, took the first boat away.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker-framed craft paddled on Welsh and Irish rivers.

clue.text: Fair is too foul an _____ for thee" (Marlowe).

definitions.text: Fair is too foul an _____ for thee" (Marlowe).

parts.words: Fair is too foul an _____ for thee" (Marlowe).
parts.note: a line of Marlowe with one word blanked out: the missing word is a descriptive label, here 'fair', applied to a beloved

explanation.definitionFit: The blank is a descriptive term or label; the speaker finds the adjective 'fair' too poor to describe the beloved.

clue.text: Abstract expressionism, initially free from vagueness

parts.note: an abstract is a summary, also called a précis

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of expressionism

explanation.surface: Abstract expressionism, in its early days, steered clear of fuzziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract expressionism' reads as the art movement, but it splits into a summary and one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact, sharply defined statements leave nothing unclear.

clue.text: Bishop is underground party man but not here in France

parts.note: the Paris underground railway is the Métro

indicators.note: but not means these letters are taken away

parts.note: a politician is a member of a party
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A bishop is a secret party member, though not in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes ICI from POLITICIAN, leaving POLITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop heading an ecclesiastical province holds this title.
